report.summary: Three findings: highest priority is a new unmodeled egress of Confidential order data (customer email) to a third-party hosted analytics collector that has no external element, flow, or third-party dependency in the checkout DFD.

findings.title: New external analytics collector and outbound flow missing from the 'checkout' DFD

model_excerpt.quote: data_flow_diagram_v2 "checkout" { process "Web App"; external_element "Customer"; data_store "Orders Database"; flow "https": Customer -> Web App; flow "sql": Web App -> Orders Database }

evidence.note: New constant analyticsURL points at https://collector.example-analytics.com/v1/events, an external host absent from the DFD
http.Post sends order events out of the service — a new outbound flow crossing the trust boundary
Store.Create now invokes publishAnalytics on every order creation, so the flow is on the primary checkout path

relevance.justification: The DFD enumerates exactly three nodes and two flows; the diff introduces a third-party destination and a new outbound flow that the diagram does not contain.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: in the data_flow_diagram_v2 "checkout" block, add an external_element for the hosted analytics collector (https://collector.example-analytics.com/v1/events, referenced at internal/orders/analytics.go:9) and a flow from process "Web App" to that external element named e.g. "analytics-events", with information_asset = "order-history" since the payload includes o.CustomerEmail and o.AmountCents (internal/orders/analytics.go:13-18). This flow was added in this PR by publishAnalytics, called from Store.Create at internal/orders/orders.go:8.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an external_element for the analytics collector and a Web App -> collector flow carrying 'order-history' to the checkout DFD.

findings.title: Hosted analytics service is a new third-party data processor with no third_party_dependency assertion

model_excerpt.quote: threat_model "checkout service" { ... } // no third_party_dependency blocks declared

evidence.note: Code calls an externally hosted SaaS endpoint (collector.example-analytics.com) not declared anywhere in the model
Confidential customer email is included in the payload sent to that third party

relevance.justification: The model declares zero third-party dependencies, yet the service now transmits confidential customer data to an external vendor on every order.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: add a third_party_dependency block for the hosted analytics service at https://collector.example-analytics.com/v1/events (introduced in internal/orders/analytics.go:9-23). Describe that order events containing customer email addresses and amounts are transmitted to it, reference information_asset "order-history", and set uptime_dependency appropriately (the call is best-effort — failures are only logged at internal/orders/orders.go:9).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third_party_dependency block for the hosted analytics collector, noting it receives 'order-history' data.

findings.title: 'order-history' asset and 'order database exposure' threat assume order data stays in the database

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "order-history" classification=Confidential — Customer orders, including email addresses and amounts, in the orders database

evidence.note: json.Marshal builds a payload containing email and amount — the exact fields the asset describes as living in the orders database
Payload is POSTed to a third-party collector, so the asset now exists outside the database as well
Every Create call now exports the asset off-host

relevance.justification: The asset description and the only threat covering it scope exposure to the database; the diff creates a second, unmodeled location and channel for the same Confidential data.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: (1) revise the information_asset "order-history" description so it no longer claims the data lives only "in the orders database" — it is now also transmitted to a third-party analytics collector (internal/orders/analytics.go:13-22); (2) add a threat covering disclosure of order-history in transit to / at rest within that third party (STRIDE: Info Disclosure, impacts Confidentiality), since the existing threat "order database exposure" (app.tm.hcl:12) and its control "database network isolation" only address direct database access.
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden the 'order-history' asset description and add an Info Disclosure threat for order data sent to the third-party analytics service.

findings.title: New unauthenticated outbound HTTP client call with no timeout, TLS pinning, or auth modeled

model_excerpt.quote: control "database network isolation" implemented=true — The orders database accepts connections only from the web app's subnet

evidence.note: http.Post uses the default http client: no timeout, no credential, no request signing on an egress path carrying confidential data
Failures are only logged, so a hijacked or failing collector is silent to callers

relevance.justification: The model's only control is inbound database network isolation; it says nothing about egress paths, and this new one has no controls asserted at all.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: under the new third-party analytics threat, add control blocks describing how the egress call in internal/orders/analytics.go:22 is protected (TLS verification, request authentication/API key, client timeout, and data minimisation such as omitting o.CustomerEmail). Mark implemented = false for any control not present in the code today — the current call uses http.Post with the default client and no credentials.
findings.suggested_fix: Add controls (TLS/auth/timeout/data minimisation) for the analytics egress call and mark unimplemented ones implemented = false.
